nodes.description: Glutathione is exported from cells and filtered at the glomerulus, and is normally degraded at the luminal brush border of the renal proximal tubule, where GGT is concentrated. Without GGT, filtered and circulating glutathione cannot be broken down for recovery of its constituent amino acids. Older work proposed that the gamma-glutamyl cycle mediates amino-acid transport, but GGT-deficient patients have normal plasma amino acids and renal amino-acid reabsorption, and the extracellular hydrolysis of glutathione is now regarded as the enzyme's physiological role.

evidence.snippet: It now appears that the activities attributed to the gamma-glutamyl cycle do not participate in amino acid transport, but instead constitute three separate metabolic pathways; the intracellular synthesis of glutathione, the intracellular degradation of gamma-glutamyl peptides and the extracellular hydrolysis of glutathione.

nodes.description: GGT1 is an extracellular, plasma-membrane-anchored enzyme that hydrolyses or transfers the gamma-glutamyl moiety of glutathione and other gamma-glutamyl compounds; it catalyses the first step of glutathione degradation. In the one molecularly characterised family a homozygous 16.9 kb intragenic GGT1 deletion abolishes it. Activity in affected individuals is very low or below detection in serum, but is not completely absent in all patients studied, consistent with contributions from other members of the GGT gene family.

nodes.description: Five of the seven patients counted in a 2007 review had central nervous system involvement (intellectual disability, developmental delay, behavioural problems), and the two genetically confirmed siblings have mild psychomotor delay and mild neurological symptoms. This figure is strongly shaped by ascertainment: the disorder is found by measuring glutathione, which is not part of routine screening, and the early patients were found during metabolic investigation of intellectual disability. No genotype-first or otherwise unselected series exists, so there is no way yet to tell how often a deficient individual is neurologically normal. The review authors state that whether the neurological symptoms are part of the disease remains to be established.

nodes.description: In GGT-deficient mice, chronic urinary loss of glutathione deprives tissues of the cysteine normally recovered from extracellular glutathione, and liver and lens glutathione fall; cysteine-prodrug supplementation reverses the mouse phenotype. This node is supported in mice only. In patients, cellular glutathione is reported to be normal, and no human counterpart of the mouse growth failure, cataract or infertility has been reported, so the node is recorded with contradicting human evidence rather than as an established human mechanism.
